completion_promises.criterion_text: In-process NATS test server fixture in tests/conftest.py (or a feature-local conftest) — reusable, port=0 so the OS picks a free port.
completion_promises.evidence: Added `nats_test_server`, `nats_server_binary`, and `_free_tcp_port` fixtures to tests/conftest.py. The fixture spawns `nats-server -p <free> -a 127.0.0.1 -js -sd <tmp>` as a subprocess (port discovered via socket bind to port 0), poll-connects until ready (5s budget), yields a connected NATSClient wrapper, and cleanly drains + terminates on teardown. If `nats-server` is missing from PATH, the fixture raises pytest.skip('install nats-server CLI for integration tests'). Reusable across the suite (any future integration test can request the same fixture).

completion_promises.criterion_text: All scenarios above covered with one test function each.
completion_promises.evidence: tests/test_fleet_registration_integration.py covers the 4 fleet scenarios: register-then-query, heartbeat-fires-at-interval, deregister-removes-entry, register-then-register-again-idempotent. tests/test_capabilities_real.py covers the 4 capabilities scenarios: pre-seeded-specialists-listed, kv-watch-invalidates-on-registration, kv-watch-invalidates-on-deregistration, capabilities_refresh-forces-immediate-reread. Each scenario is exactly one test function.

completion_promises.criterion_text: No GB10 / external NATS dependency — pure portable tests.
completion_promises.evidence: All NATS I/O routes through the in-process subprocess broker bound to a tmp_path JetStream store directory. No reference to GB10 (100.84.90.91) or external broker addresses. The fixture uses `nats://127.0.0.1:<free_port>` exclusively. No .creds file, no Tailscale, no external network requirement.

Each test gets a fresh subprocess broker (function-scoped fixture) and a fresh JetStream store dir under tmp_path — no fixture state outlives a single test. The capabilities tests rebind the module-level `_capability_registry` and use a `restore_capability_registry` snapshot/restore fixture so the binding is restored on teardown. Verified ordering-invariance by running the suite in both forward and reverse module order — both passed (8/8 each). pytest-randomly is not installed in the environment but the isolation contract is independently satisfied by per-test fixture scoping.

Verified: `uv run pytest tests/test_fleet_registration_integration.py tests/test_capabilities_real.py -v` yields '8 passed in 17.80s' against an installed nats-server (v2.12.8 via brew). On systems lacking the binary the suite cleanly skips with the documented operator hint.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Subjects asserted via nats_core.Topics.* formatters (no hard-coded literals in the assertions).
completion_promises.evidence: Both test files import `from nats_core.topics import Topics` and anchor subject-related assertions against `Topics.Fleet.REGISTER` and `Topics.Fleet.DEREGISTER`. The agent-registry KV bucket name is anchored against `nats_core.client.AGENT_REGISTRY_BUCKET` rather than the literal 'agent-registry'. No fleet/agents subject literals appear in assertion expressions.

`nats_test_server` is decorated with `@pytest_asyncio.fixture()`. Every async test function in both new test files carries `@pytest.mark.asyncio` even though `asyncio_mode = 'auto'` is configured (explicit decorators per the task requirement). pytest_asyncio is imported at the top of tests/conftest.py.
